Python has no true constant construct; `counter = 0` and `LIMIT = 100` are syntactically identical simple assignments, so which one is 'immutable by convention' is not locally determinate from the two declarations alone.
Both branches assign an int literal before use; definite assignment is locally verifiable, no separate uninitialized-declare form exists in Python.
bytearray(16) is spec-guaranteed zero-filled (Python provides no genuinely uninitialized buffer); substituted fragment is fully determinate.
x += 1 on unbounded Python int: no overflow, single deterministic outcome.
xs[1] = 42 on a list is always an in-place element mutation by spec.
`is` vs `==` is a hard language distinction; identity test is unambiguous.

Bare f(x): Python's uniform call-by-object-reference rules out 'callee cannot observe x' and 'a copy was made' outright, but read-only vs in-place mutation vs alias retention beyond the call remain undecidable without consulting f; 3 of the 6 listed outcomes survive.
Closure capturing k and map(neg, xs) is fully local, deterministic Python closure semantics.
Elements are ints (immutable); aliasing vs copying the returned element is not materially distinguishable.
Tuple return (a//b, a%b) is Python's single standard multi-value mechanism.
a*b+c: fixed precedence, unbounded int, no ambiguity.
//, %, and / are individually fully spec-defined (floor division, sign-follows-divisor remainder, true division to float).
Explicit b==0 guard (rung ii, since no stdlib checked-division exists) is fully deterministic.
str.__eq__ is spec-defined content equality, not identity.
Whichever of sorted()/list.sort() R10 selects has fully documented in-place-vs-new-list behavior.
ctypes.c_int32(big).value is a deterministic, documented wraparound conversion.
int+float promotion to float is a fixed Python arithmetic rule.
xs[i] out-of-range deterministically raises IndexError.
List slicing always copies by language spec; no ambiguity.
o = None then conditional fallback; None is the explicit, unambiguous absent sentinel at this site.
Substituted explicit conditional (Python has no Optional-map operator) is fully explicit.
int(s) raising ValueError and propagating on an unhandled path is Python's uniform exception model.
try/except ValueError with fallback is fully explicit and deterministic.
Python enforces no sealed/closed alternative sets; a Union-typed class hierarchy could in principle be extended, so 'closed' vs 'open' is not locally decidable from the declaration alone.
match without a wildcard arm has one deterministic behavior on non-match (falls through, no exception) under Python's documented match-statement semantics.
Dispatch is always dynamic single-mechanism (duck typing / MRO); no alternative interpretation.
Python functions are implicitly parametric; no generic-declaration ambiguity.
No declared constraint exists; misuse deterministically surfaces at call time via TypeError under Python's fixed duck-typing model.
Heterogeneous list + dynamic dispatch is Python's single, uniform mechanism.
sum(xs) over an int list is fully spec-defined.
dict iteration order is insertion order (guaranteed since 3.7) and .get(key, default) is deterministic.
with-statement guarantees __exit__/close on every exit path, including exceptions; fully deterministic.
Using an explicit scoped construct (with-block invoking a documented close(), not relying on __del__) yields deterministic, single-interpretation cleanup timing.
print is a builtin requiring no import; single deterministic form.
A leading underscore is a documented convention, not enforcement; the resulting accessibility fact is itself a single deterministic Python-spec fact, not an open branch.
asyncio.gather over two coroutines has fully documented cooperative single-thread join semantics.
Cooperative single-threaded asyncio execution with no await inside the increment is documented to make the read-modify-write atomic; deterministic.
